profile.name: Carl Lambrecht
profile.bio: Carl Lambrecht is a business owner who has run the optics manufacturer Laurel Industries since 1978 and holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois. He ran unsuccessfully for the Illinois House in 2024.
profile.notes: No campaign website or issue positions were found. Sources differ on which Illinois House district he ran in during 2024.

profile.name: Julie Fortier
profile.bio: Julie Fortier is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 12th congressional district in 2026. Public information about her background was not found in the sources reviewed.
profile.notes: No campaign website, biography or issue statements could be located; Ballotpedia was not reachable during research.

profile.name: Dillan Vancil
profile.current_role: Railroad union official and small-business owner
profile.bio: Dillan Vancil is a railroad worker from west-central Illinois and state legislative director for the SMART-TD rail union. He owns a coffee shop business and serves as vice president of the West Central school board and on the Eagle View Health System board.

platform.point: Wants to bring manufacturing jobs back to Illinois and support small businesses.
Pledges to support Illinois workers and labor organisations.
Calls for price transparency in health care.
Aims to secure student funding and education access for rural communities.

profile.notes: Campaign priorities are too general to score.

profile.name: Lupe Castillo
profile.bio: Lupe Castillo is a pharmacy technician and the 2026 Republican nominee in Illinois's 4th district. Castillo also ran for this seat in 2024.
profile.notes: No campaign website or issue statements were found; Ballotpedia pages could not be loaded.

profile.name: Chad Koppie
profile.bio: Chad Koppie is a farmer from northern Illinois and a retired Delta Air Lines captain who trained at Purdue University's aviation school. He has served on the Kane County Regional Board of Schools, a local school board and as a township trustee, and was the Republican nominee for this seat in earlier cycles.

platform.point: Names banning abortion as the main goal of his campaign.
Cut federal spending substantially and lower tax rates.
Build a border wall and have ICE arrest and deport all people in the country illegally.
Reduce federal government power, which he describes as a threat to liberty.

economy.evidence: Calls for large spending cuts and lower tax rates.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion and pledges to protect all human life (abortion), and as a lifetime NRA member pledges to defend the Second Amendment (guns).

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall and deportation of all undocumented immigrants.

profile.notes: Abortion and immigration positions come from 2022-2024 coverage and questionnaires. The campaign headshot is hosted on his older chadkoppie.com domain.

profile.name: Barb Regnitz
profile.bio: Barb Regnitz is a Porter County commissioner from Valparaiso who won the Republican nomination for Indiana's 1st district in May 2026. She holds Purdue degrees in mathematics and German and worked as a software engineer and project manager and later as a certified financial planner.

platform.point: Supports law enforcement and wants to end catch-and-release practices.
Makes securing the border one of the main planks of her platform.
Wants to reduce federal spending and the national debt.
Backs in-person voting and watermarked paper ballots as election-integrity measures.
Wants schools to focus on teaching students how to think rather than what to think.
Supports reserving girls' sports and facilities for biological females.

economy.evidence: Platform calls for reducing federal spending and the national debt.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: supports limiting girls' sports and facilities to biological females; no public stance found on abortion, guns or drugs.

immigration.evidence: Calls for ending catch-and-release policies and securing the border.

profile.notes: The campaign website did not render for review, so the platform comes from WFYI's primary guide; scores rest on a few planks.

profile.name: Patrick McAuley
profile.bio: Patrick McAuley is the Republican nominee for Indiana's 7th district in Indianapolis. His campaign says he wants to work with local, state and federal leaders to bring more financial resources into the district's communities.

platform.point: Wants stronger community-police relationships, more officers in neighborhoods and targeted crime-reduction resources.
Proposes expanding housing supply and reusing vacant buildings to address rising rents.
Supports partnerships and federal resources to help people move off the street.
Prioritises vocational training and apprenticeships as paths to skilled jobs for young people.

security.evidence: Calls for increasing police officer presence in neighborhoods alongside community policing.

profile.notes: Little biographical information is published; security score added from his public-safety platform.

profile.name: Don Coover
profile.bio: Don Coover grew up on a family farm in rural southeast Kansas and served more than ten years as a U.S. Army officer, including as an infantry officer and Army aviator. A Kansas State University veterinary graduate, he has run a livestock veterinary practice and a working cattle ranch and co-founded agricultural businesses. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Focus on bringing down grocery and housing costs for working families.
Work to keep local hospitals in rural Kansas from closing.
Treat farm policy as central to food prices and grocery bills.
Reduce partisan gridlock and have Washington spend within its means.

profile.notes: Faces incumbent Republican Derek Schmidt; campaign site lists themes but no concrete policy positions, so no domain is scored.
